findings.finding: Compensation of Employees 124.1 Non-Compliance with the Law on Fiscal Responsibility – Wage Bill The statements of receipts and payments reflects an expenditure of Kshs.480,715,437 on compensation of employees representing 51% of the total receipts of Kshs.947,936,408. This is contrary to the provisions of Regulation 25 (1)(b) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which limits for expenditure on wages and benefits to not more than 35% of the county government’s total revenue for the year. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law. 124.2 Non-Compliance with Law on Ethnic Composition During the year under review, the total number of employees in the County Assembly was seventy-four (74) out of which, seventy-one (71) or 96 % of the total number were members of the dominant ethnic community in the county. This is contrary to Section 7(1) and (2) of the National Cohesion and Integration Act, 2008 which states that, “all public offices shall seek to represent the diversity of the people of Kenya in employment of staff and that no public institution shall have more than one third of its staff establishment from the same ethnic community”. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Late Disbursement of Funds As disclosed in Note 1 to the financial statements, the statement of receipts and payments for the year ended 30 June, 2021 reflects Kshs.947,936,408 in respect to transfers from the County Treasury which includes Kshs.152,441,408 transferred between 02 July, 2021 and 09 July, 2021 after the closure of the financial year on 30 June, 2021 contrary to Section 97(1) of the Public Finance Management Act (County Governments) Regulations 2015 which states that the accounts of county government entities shall record transactions which take place during a financial year running from the 1 July to the 30 June under the cash basis of accounting. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Ward Operating Expenses As disclosed in Note 4 to the financial statements, the statement of receipts and payments reflects Kshs.416,097,371 relating to use of goods and services. This amount includes Kshs.64,269,561 on account of other operating expenses which further includes Kshs.18,486,286 issued as imprest to forty-five (45) wards and twenty-two (22) nominated MCAs. However, review of the imprest surrender vouchers revealed the following: - i) There was no structure for procurement of most of the common user items in these wards contrary to Section 33(3) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which states that “the County Treasury may prescribe an institutional framework to provide for the procurement, administration and management of common user items for the county government.” As a result, the wards had uncontrolled and unguided spending on these items, each sourcing directly for the items, contrary to the provisions of Article 227(1) of the Constitution which requires that when a public entity contracts for goods or services, it shall do so in accordance with a system that is fair, equitable, transparent, competitive and cost-effective. ii) Some of the receipts used for surrender of government funds were doubtful as they were not serialised, did not bear the dates, handwriting seemed similar, did not bear the official details of the merchants from whom the wards procured items and they did not bear the tax registration details of the merchants, thereby possibly denying the government tax revenue. iii) An abstract and analysis of the memorandum cash books for all wards and nominated Members of County Assembly were not provided for audit contrary to Regulation 93(15) of the Public Finance and Management (County Governments) Regulation, 2015, which states that when the imprest holder needs to have his or her funds replenished, he or she shall send an abstract and analysis of his or her memorandum cash book, plus originals of the supporting payment vouchers to accounts division. In the circumstances, the propriety and accuracy for the expenditures of Kshs.18,486,286 for the year ended 30 June, 2021 could not be confirmed.

Unresolved Prior Year Audit Matters In the audit report of the previous year, several issues were raised under the Report on Financial Statements, Report on Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and Report on Effectiveness of Internal Controls, Risk Management and Governance. However, no report or recommendations from the County Assembly Management and oversight bodies were provided for audit verification. Further, the issues remained unresolved contrary to Section 149(2)(l) of the Public Finance Management Act, 2012 which require Accounting Officers designated for county government entities to try to resolve any issues resulting from an audit that remain outstanding.

Accuracy of the Financial Statements The statement of receipts and payments for the year under review reflects a balance of Kshs.23,132,741 in respect to transfer to other government entities. However, the statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts recurrent and development combined reflects an amount of Kshs.20,445,542 in respect to transfer to other government entities resulting to an unexplained variance of Kshs.2,687,199. In addition, the statement of comparison of budget and actual amounts reflects a budgeted final exchequer releases amount of Kshs.917,309,532. However, a recast of the receipts amounted to shs.917,669,532 thereby resulting to an unexplained variance of Kshs.360,000. Further, Notes 3 and 4 to the financial statements reflect Kshs.480,715,437 and Kshs.416,097,371 in respect to compensation of employees and use of goods and services respectively. However, a recast of the expenditure amounted to Kshs.480,718,437 and Kshs.411,292,221 resulting to unexplained variances of Kshs.3,000 and Kshs.4,805,150 respectively. In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the balances reported in the financial statements for the year ended 30 June, 2021 could not be confirmed.

Compensation of Employees - Use of a Manual Payroll As disclosed in Note 3 to the financial statements, the statement of receipts and payments for the year ended 30 June, 2021 reflects Kshs.480,715,437 in respect to compensation of employees. However, records provided revealed that out of the amount of Kshs.480,715,437, an amount of Kshs.47,315,380 was paid to two hundred and seven (207) ward offices’ employees through the manual payroll during the year ended 30 June, 2021. This is contrary to the requirement of Section 12(1)(e) of the Public Finance Management Act, 2012 which states that subject to the Constitution and this Act, the National Treasury shall design and prescribe an efficient financial management system for the national and county governments to ensure transparent financial management and standard financial reporting as contemplated by Article 226 of the Constitution. In the circumstances, the accuracy of the compensation of employee’s expenditure through manual payroll of Kshs.47,315,380 in the financial statements for the year ended 30 June, 2021 could not be confirmed.

Acquisition of Assets - Delayed Delivery of the Speaker’s Vehicle As disclosed in Note 6 to the financial statements, the statement of receipts and payments for the year ended 30 June, 2021 reflects Kshs.30,628,234 in respect to acquisition of assets, which includes Kshs.14,249,995 for purchase of a motor vehicle for the County Assembly Speaker. The vehicle was procured from a local car dealer based on the Ministry of Transport, Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development and Public Works Contract Agreement, and payment was made on 16 November, 2020. However, at the time of audit exercise in October, 2021, the vehicle had not been delivered to the County Assembly contrary to Section 146 of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Failure to Prepare and Publish Contract Awards Management did not prepare, publish and publicize all contract awards as required contrary to Section 138(1) and (2) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which stipulates that the accounting officer of a procuring entity shall publish and publicize all contract awards on their notice boards at conspicuous places, and website if available within a period as prescribed and that an accounting officer of a procuring entity shall report all contract awards to the Authority as prescribed. Further, monthly progress reports on implementation of procurement contracts were not provided for audit. As a result, there was no confirmation that Management monitored implementation of contracts regularly as required contrary to Section 152 of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which stipulates that the head of the procurement function shall prepare monthly progress reports of all procurement contracts of the procuring entity and submit them to the Accounting Officer. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Lack of Risk Management Policy for Internal Audit The County Executive did not have a Risk Management Policy contrary to Regulation 153(1)(b) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which requires that internal auditors shall have a duty to give reasonable assurance through the Audit Committee on the state of risk management, control and governance within the organization. In the circumstances, existence of an effective risk management system could not be confirmed.

Renewal of Insurance Policy for Provision of Medical Cover and WIBA Policy The County Executive entered into a contract for renewal of an insurance cover for the provision of medical insurance and WIBA policy cover on 18 December, 2020 at a total premium cost of Kshs.279,984,357. The renewal was to cover a period of one (1) year commencing on 23 December, 2020 and ending on 22 December, 2021. The Tender Evaluation Committee deliberated on the proposal and recommended for the renewal of medical insurance and WIBA policy contract from an amount of Kshs.249,876,345 in the financial year 2019/2020 to an amount of Kshs.279,984,357 in the financial year 2020/2021. The Committee further noted that the variation of the tender by a total of Kshs.30,108,012, which is a 12% increase from the previous contract cost, was within the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015. However, no evidence was provided by Management to show that a market survey was carried out to show that the offer provided by the insurance company was at the prevailing market prices. This was contrary to Regulation 90(1)(d)(ii) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Regulations, 2020 which states that an accounting officer shall not enter into a contract under Section 104 of the Act unless it is satisfied that the offer is at the prevailing real market price. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Lack of Approved Budget and Procurement Plan - Facility Improvement Fund (FIF) Note 11 to the financial statements reflects other payments of Kshs.1,762,073,031 which includes other expenses - FIF of Kshs.250,418,541 which were incurred without an approved budget by both the County Executive Committee and County Assembly since the only budget that was presented to County Assembly on Ministry of Health expenditure was on recurrent and development expenditures in the 2020/2021 financial year. Further the FIF did not have a procurement plan contrary to Section 53(2) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which requires the Accounting Officer to prepare an annual procurement plan within the approved budget prior to commencement of each financial year as part of the annual budget preparation process. It was also noted that the County Health Management Board was not in place to approve budgets for individual health facilities contrary to the guidelines from the Ministry of Health issued in 2014. In addition, individual work plans for each Hspital with specific parameters and approved budget for each health facility were not provided for audit. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Irregular Contract Agreement Note 11 to the financial statements reflects a total of Kshs.1,762,073,031 in respect to other payments which includes an amount of Kshs.1,437,584,826 in respect to other expenses - payables from previous financial period which further includes an amount of Kshs.4,247,461 paid by Department of Water to a contractor for installation of pipes. However, the contract agreement between the contractor and County Executive was entered on the same day the notification of award was issued. This was contrary to Section 135 (3) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015 which states that the written contract shall be entered into within the period specified in the notification but not before fourteen days have elapsed following the giving of that notification provided that a contract shall be signed within the tender validity period. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Construction of Deputy Governor’s Residence Other expenses - payables from previous financial period includes an amount of Kshs.27,798,711 paid to a construction company for the construction of Deputy Governor’s residence being the payment certificates No.2, 3 and 4. Review of the project documents indicated that the contract period was 24 weeks from 15 October, 2018 to 14 April, 2019. However, a second contract extension was granted and the revised completion date was 28 December, 2021. Further, physical verification carried out in October, 2021 revealed that the boundary wall was still in progress and was approximately 80% done, the DSQ and guard house were incomplete with electrical works, plumbing works and exterior paintwork outstanding while tiling and cabinets for the main house kitchen, external paintworks, external civil works, cabro laying, drainage and parking bays had not been done. In addition, the contractor’s revised program of works to cover the extended timelines was not provided for audit. In the circumstances, the value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.27,798,711 could not be confirmed.

Stalled Construction of Office Block The County Executive entered into a contract for construction of low-cost office block at the Meru County Public Works Headquarters with a contractor on the 28 July, 2020 at a contract sum of Kshs.10,424,273. The contract was to run for a period of twenty-four (24) weeks upto 31 January, 2021. During the year under review, an amount of Kshs.6,133,503 which included a balance of Kshs.3,990,992 relating to payables from previous financial period - others (budget) and an amount of Kshs,2,142,511 relating to residential buildings (including hostels), was paid to the contractor. Audit verification on the progress of work revealed that the contractor was not on site and the contract period had already elapsed. Further, it was noted that fixing of glazed metal door, interior flush doors, tiling, paintwork, fixing of steel windows, fixing of portable fire extinguishers, ceiling, sanitary, plumbing and drainage works, and landscaping had not commenced although they had been provided for in the bill of quantities. In addition, the contractor used interlocking stones for external walling instead of “200 mm rough dressed natural stone” as specified in the bill of quantities. Further, an updated program of works as approved by the Project Manager and minutes of Project Inspection Team were not provided for audit contrary to contractual obligations. No explanations were provided on the action taken by County Executive against the contractor despite default in executing the contractual obligations. In the circumstances, the value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.6,133,503 incurred on this project could not be confirmed.

Construction of Governor’s Residence As disclosed in Note 11 to the financial statements, the statement of receipts and payments reflects other payments of Kshs.1,762,073,031 which include an amount of Kshs.1,437,584,826 in respect to other expenses - payables from previous financial period. This latter amount includes an expenditure of Kshs.54,567,213 paid to a construction company for the construction of Governor’s residence being the payment certificates No. 2, 3 4 and 5. Review of the project documents provided for audit indicated the contract period was 24 weeks from 15 October, 2018 to 14 April, 2019. However, a second contract extension was requested by the contractor on 17 July, 2021 and granted by the County Executive on the 16 August, 2021 with the revised completion date of 28 December, 2021. Further, physical verification carried out in October, 2021 revealed that the door for the generator room, ceiling and tiling, the electrical works for the Governor offices, external civil works, drainage works and cabro laying had not been done while paintworks was still in progress. In addition, the contractor’s revised program of works to cater for the extended timelines up to contract conclusion was not provided for audit. In the circumstances, the value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.54,567,213 could not be confirmed.

Underpayment of Salary Review of manual payroll revealed that two (2) staff members in different job groups had an annual basic salary of Kshs.141,445 each which was below the minimum limit of Kshs.200,790 set by Salaries and Remuneration Commission (SRC) resulting to an underpayment of an amount of Kshs.59,345. This was contrary to the Salaries and Remuneration (SRC) Circular dated 8 July, 2020 which categorized job groups and their basic pay bands to be adopted by the County Government. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Irregular Probation Period Review of manual payroll and samples of personal files for contract staff revealed that thirteen (13) officers were on probation for more than six (6) months. This was contrary to Section B.16 (1) of the Human Resource Policies and Procedures Manual for the Public Service, 2016 which states that where vacancies exist in the pensionable establishment, candidates recruited to fill such vacancies shall be appointed on probation for a period of six (6) months. In circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Non-Compliance with the One Third Basic Salary Rule Review of the monthly payroll records revealed that some employees’ salary deductions fell below 1/3 of the basic salary. This was contrary to the provisions of Section 19 (3) of the Employment Act, 2007 which requires that deductions made by an employer from the wages of his employee at any one time shall not exceed two thirds of such wages. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Lack of an Approved Staff Establishment During the audit, it was noted that the County Executive did not have an approved staff establishment. This was contrary to the requirements of Section B 5(2) of the County Public Service Human Resource Manual, 2013 which states that all vacancies shall be declared in a prescribed format which shall include the number of vacancies; when the vacancy occurred; whether the vacancy is within the authorized establishment and other relevant details. Further, Section B 6(3) states that in the recruitment process, due consideration will be given to appropriate organizational structure in each Department, optimal staffing levels, schemes of service and career progression guidelines. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Non-Compliance with the Law on Fiscal Responsibility - Wage Bill The statement of receipts and payments reflects an expenditure of Kshs.4,450,390,659 on compensation of employees representing 42% of the total receipts of Kshs.10,694,908,070. This is contrary to the provisions of Regulation 25 (1) (b) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which limits for expenditure on wages and benefits to not more than 35% of the County Government’s total revenue for the year. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Irregular Procurement of Sports Equipments The County Executive initiated the procurement process for purchase of sports equipment for the Governor’s Cup on the 23 April, 2021 through a request in line with the provisions of Section 60(1) of the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal, 2015. The Local Purchase Order (LPO) in respect to this procurement, which had a total contract cost of Kshs.2,970,000, was issued to the supplier on the 16 June, 2021. However, the following observations have been made regarding the procurement: (i). The nature of the event necessitating the procurement, details of the intended users and work plan for the sports activity were not supported by any documentary evidence. The user department did not provide the specific requirements in respect to this procurement especially regarding sizes of soccer boots. (ii). Although the goods were delivered and taken charge to the stores, Management did not facilitate independent audit verification of the items. (iii). No evidence was provided to confirm that the items were issued to the intended users. Further, during the year under review, the supplier was also awarded a contract to supply branded football and goalkeeper uniforms at a contract price of Kshs.2,536,000. However, the specifications issued by the user department lacked a description of the sizes of different attires a clear indication that the intended users had not been identified. In addition, no evidence was provided to confirm the issuance of the uniforms to the intended users. In the circumstances, it was not possible to determine whether the public got value for money from the expenditure totalling to Kshs.5,506,000.

Unutilized Water Project Management entered into a contract with a contractor for construction and rehabilitation of Runogone Water Project at a contract sum of Kshs.7,321,000. However, physical verification of the project revealed that the project was not operational despite the works having been certified complete and fully paid for. Further, it was noted that there were cases of vandalism of the pipes along the roadside. In addition, it was noted the piped water which was to flow by gravity did not flow as required, which was an indication that the project’s feasibility study was poorly done. In the circumstances, the value for money for the expenditure on the Project could not be confirmed.

Unauthorized Opening of Bank Accounts As disclosed in Note 12A to the financial statements, the statement of assets and liabilities reflects bank balances of Kshs.1,969,050,306 held in thirty-seven (37) bank accounts operated by the County Executive out of which twenty-four (24) were held in various commercial bank accounts. This was contrary to Regulation 82(1)(b) and (5) of the Public Finance Management (County Governments) Regulations, 2015 which stipulates that all County Government bank accounts shall be opened at the Central Bank of Kenya except for imprest bank accounts for petty cash. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Irregular Payment of Allowances to Members of County Assembly (MCAs) As disclosed in Note 6 to the financial statements, the statement of receipts and payments reflects use of goods and services expenditure of Kshs.1,226,954,795 which includes an amount of Kshs.186,525,557 in respect to domestic travel and subsistence. The latter amount includes an expenditure of Kshs.9,699,800 paid to MCAs as per diem and transport allowances while attending various Committee Meetings of the County Executive. However, the MCAs have their budgetary allocation for domestic travel and subsistence under the County Assembly. In addition, there was conflict of interest since the County Assembly is supposed to play an oversight role, yet the members of its committees are involved in discussing and report writing for various departments of the County Executive. In the circumstances, the propriety and value for money for the expenditure of Kshs.9,699,800 could not be confirmed.

Unremitted Statutory Deductions Note 5 to the financial statements reflects compensation of employees payments of Kshs.4,450,390,659 which includes an amount of Kshs.2,037,151,404 and Kshs.140,298,937 in respect to basic pay of permanent and temporary employees respectively and an amount of Kshs.236,014,615 in respect to pension and other social security contributions. Review of records revealed that an amount of Kshs.67,444,200 and Kshs.3,777,200 was deducted from various officers during the year in respect to National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) and National Social Security Fund (NSSF) respectively. However, the County Executive only provided evidence of remittance of Kshs.3,307,598 in respect to NHIF and Kshs.2,459,200 in respect to NSSF thereby resulting to unremitted deductions of Kshs.64,136,602 and Kshs.1,318,000 for NHIF and NSSF respectively. This was contrary to Section 16(1) of the National Hospital Insurance Fund Cap 255 of the Laws of Kenya, which states that a person liable to pay a standard contribution under section 15 shall pay such contribution through monthly deductions from his salary or other remuneration and the employer of such person shall be liable to deduct and to pay the contribution to the Board on behalf of and to the exclusion of that person. Further, Section 20 of the National Social Security Fund Act, 2013 which states that an employer shall make mandatory contributions to the Fund as defined in the Act. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.

Unresolved Prior Year Audit Matters In the audit report of the previous year, several issues were raised under the Report on Financial Statements, Report on Lawfulness and Effectiveness in Use of Public Resources, and Report on Effectiveness of Internal Controls, Risk Management and Governance. However, no report or recommendations from the County Executive Management and oversight bodies were submitted for audit verification. Further, the issues remained unresolved without satisfactory explanation.

Pending Bills According to Annex 2 to the financial statements, the County Executive had pending accounts payable totalling to Kshs.1,096,419,204 as at 30 June, 2021. Management has not explained why the bills were not settled during the year when they occurred. The County Executive is at risk of incurring significant interest costs and penalties with their continued delay in payment. Failure to settle bills during the year to which they relate to distorts the financial statements and adversely affects the budgetary provisions for the subsequent year as they form a first charge.

Fixed Asset Register Annex 6 to the financial statements reflects a balance of Kshs.7,730,379,420 in respect to the historical cost of the summary of non-current asset register as at 30 June, 2021. This balance includes assets balalnce of Kshs.686,572,764 described as transport equipment, whose breakdown showing the details and specific location of the assets, and ownership documents were not provided for audit. Further, included in the total assets historical cost of Kshs.7,730,379,420 is a balance of Kshs.42,337,783 relating to the historical cost of land. However, the County Executive did not provide a list of all parcels of land owned by the County, details of the specific location of land, approximate size, value of land and the respective title deeds/ownership documents. In the circumstances, the existence, accuracy and completeness of the historical cost balance of Kshs.7,730,379,420 in respect to the summary of non-current assets register could not be confirmed.

Inaccuracies in the Statement of Receipts and Payments The statement of receipts and payments does not reflect any miscellaneous receipts, while supporting documents provided for audit reflect an amount of Kshs.3,871,923 under miscellaneous receipts. Further, Note 8 to the financial statements reflects other grants and capital transfers amount of Kshs.807,944,164, which differs with the supporting schedule amount of Kshs.807,854,363 by an unexplained variance of Kshs.89,801. In addition, Note 11 to the financial statements reflects an other payments amount of Kshs.1,762,073,031 which includes other expenses - payables from the previous financial year expenditure of Kshs.1,437,584,826. This latter amount however differs with the supporting records amount of Kshs.1,454,584,827 by an unexplained amount of Kshs.17,000,001. In the circumstances, the accuracy of the statement of receipts and payments balances could not be confirmed.

Unsupported Acquisition of Assets As disclosed in Note 10 to the financial statements, the statement of receipts and payments reflects acquisition of assets expenditure of Kshs.619,093,233. This expenditure includes construction of buildings expenditure of Kshs.100,272,947 which further includes an expenditure of Kshs.12,000,000 which was transferred by the County Executive to Meru County Micro-Finance Corporation to boost small and micro traders and which ought to have been classified as transfers to other Government entities and therefore overstating the construction of buildings amount. In addition, the amount of Kshs.100,272,947 includes an expenditure of Kshs.8,485,810 whose supporting documents were not provided for audit. In the circumstances, the accuracy and completeness of the construction of buildings expenditure of Kshs.100,272,947 could not be confirmed.

Non-Submission of Consolidated Annual Financial Statements Management did not prepare and submit the consolidated annual financial statements in respect of all the County Government entities and the relevant summaries to the Auditor- General and deliver a copy to the National Treasury, Controller of Budget and the Commission on Revenue Allocation. This is contrary to Section 163(1) and (4) of the Public Finance Management Act, 2012. In the circumstances, Management was in breach of the law.
